survived.title: Stepped run silently collapses to ONE atomic dispatch when every break phase is trimmed — per-group settings and group sequencing are discarded
survived.mechanism:
`_build_steps_phases` ends with a fallback:
```
if not any(p.get("phase_type") in _BREAKS or p.get("phase_type") == "zone" for p in collapsed):
    all_ids = [rid for p in collapsed for rid in p.get("queue_room_ids", [])]
    return self._build_dispatch_phases(..., managed_rooms=effective_rooms,
                                       queue_room_ids=all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids), ...)
```
Two compounding defects.

(a) `all_ids` is ALWAYS `[]`. The room_group phases in `collapsed` come from `_build_dispatch_phases` -> engine `build_payload`, and every engine returns exactly `{vacuum_entity_id, map_id, payload, resolved_rooms, room_count}` (queue_engine.py:357-363; dispatch_engines.py:211-217, 273-280, 390-396). There is no `queue_room_ids` key on a dispatch phase — only the charge_wait/wait/zone phases set it (run_plan.py:851,858,877). So `all_ids or sorted(included_room_ids)` unconditionally takes the right-hand branch.

(b) The fallback passes `managed_rooms=effective_rooms` — the GLOBAL room view — discarding the `group_managed` per-group overlay built at run_plan.py:834-841, and merges every group into a single phase.

Reachability: line 1352 only enters `_build_steps_phases` when `_run_steps` contains a charge_wait/wait/zone, but the trim at 884-887 then pops LEADING and TRAILING charge_wait/wait, and an unresolvable zone is `continue`d at 872. So a profile `[charge_wait(100), groupA, groupB]` -> after trim `[dispatchA, dispatchB]` -> no breaks -> collapse to one phase.
survived.user_impact: A saved run profile such as "charge to 100%, then bedrooms on quiet, then kitchen on max" runs as a single batch. On Roborock the per-phase `global_pre_calls` (fan / mop-intensity select, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:132-153,366) then fire ONCE max-wins over the merged room set, so the bedrooms are physically vacuumed at max suction instead of quiet — and a mixed vacuum/mop profile falls into the `mixed_mode_water_policy: safest` branch and under-mops instead of running the two groups at their own water levels. Where the same room appears in two groups ("vacuum the kitchen, then mop the kitchen" — the case _build_steps_phases exists to support) the room is dispatched ONCE with the last group's settings, so the vacuum pass never happens. No error is shown; preflight reports the run as ready.

survived.title: _match_profile_from_fields is structurally brand-blind and rewrites every Roborock room's profile_name to "custom" on every start
survived.mechanism:
`_match_profile_from_fields(self, room)` takes NO `vacuum_entity_id`, so it cannot consult the adapter. It sources candidates from `self.get_room_profiles()["profiles"]`, which calls `get_default_room_profiles()` with no catalog (profiles/manager.py:225) -> the in-code EUFY `BUILT_IN_ROOM_PROFILES`; and it resolves each candidate with `resolve_room_profile_for_room(room_config=candidate_config, stored_profiles=stored_profiles)` (manager.py:157-162) — again with no `catalog=`, so floor-type fan/water defaults are Eufy's too.

`_build_effective_start_plan` calls it on every included room while building the queue:
```
updated_room = self._manager.protected_room_config({**room_data, **updates})
matched_profile = self._manager._match_profile_from_fields(updated_room)
updated_room["profile_name"] = matched_profile if matched_profile else "custom"
effective_rooms[room_key] = updated_room
```
(run_plan.py:1309-1312). Roborock's `vacuum_quick` declares `fan_speed: "balanced"` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:114) while Eufy's declares `"Standard"`; `_normalize_profile_match_value` only lowercases (manager.py:113-135), so "balanced" != "standard" and NO profile matches -> `"custom"`. `vacuum_deep` matches only by the coincidence that both brands spell max suction "max"/"Max".

survived.title: A run profile whose first step is a zone is permanently unstartable and reports "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid"
survived.mechanism:
The leading-phase trim is deliberately narrowed to breaks only: `_BREAKS = ("charge_wait", "wait")` and `while phases and phases[0].get("phase_type") in _BREAKS: phases.pop(0)` (run_plan.py:883-885). A zone phase is therefore never trimmed, so for steps `[zone, room_group]` `phases[0]` is the zone phase, which is built as `{"phase_type": "zone", ..., "payload": {}, "room_count": 0}` (run_plan.py:873-879).

`payload_state = phases[0]` (run_plan.py:1379) then propagates a `room_count` of 0 into `get_start_status`, which passes it to `build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle(payload_room_count=int(payload_state.get("room_count", 0)))` (core/manager.py:2863) where `if int(payload_room_count or 0) <= 0:` returns `{"reason": "invalid_payload", "blocked": True}` (jobs/job_monitor.py:268-273). `start_selected_rooms` returns early on `start_status["blocked"]` (core/manager.py:4943).

The docstring three lines above the trim claims the opposite: "Leading/trailing/duplicate charge phases (nothing to bracket) are dropped so phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send" (run_plan.py:806-808). A zone IS a real clean but is not one `_dispatch_clean_payload` can send. `normalize_run_profile_steps` (profiles/manager.py:751-809) imposes no ordering constraint, so a zone-first profile is authorable and `apply_run_profile` accepts it (the room_group supplies `_profile_rooms`, so `applied` is True).
survived.user_impact: A saved run profile that begins with a saved-zone step (e.g. "spot-clean under the table, then clean the downstairs") can never be started. The user gets "Room-clean payload is missing or invalid." — a message about a corrupt payload, pointing at nothing they can fix. The feature is dead for that authoring order with no diagnostic naming the zone step.

survived.title: normalize_room_profile re-injects the Eufy literal "Quick" for clean_intensity, defeating Roborock's deliberate omission of the axis
survived.mechanism:
`normalize_room_profile` fills every key unconditionally:
```
"clean_intensity": normalize_clean_intensity(source.get("clean_intensity", d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick"))),
```
where `d = (catalog or {}).get("normalize_defaults")`. Roborock's `normalize_defaults` is `CUSTOM_ROOM_PROFILE`, which declares NO `clean_intensity` (adapters/roborock/vocabulary.py:153-162), and none of its four `ROOM_PROFILES` declare it either (vocabulary.py:110-151, with the comment at 107-109 stating the omission is deliberate: "An omitted key means the room stores nothing for it, rather than an inert 'Quick' nobody can act on"). So `d.get("clean_intensity", "Quick")` hits the hardcoded Eufy literal, and `normalize_clean_intensity("Quick")` passes it through ("quick" is not in `_DEAD_CLEAN_INTENSITY`, room_profiles.py:115-120).

Consequences: `get_room_profile` returns `normalize_room_profile(profile, catalog)` (room_profiles.py:291), so EVERY Roborock built-in comes back carrying `clean_intensity: "Quick"`; and `apply_room_profile_to_config` writes it straight onto the stored room — `updated["clean_intensity"] = normalized["clean_intensity"]` (room_profiles.py:566), reached from the apply-profile-to-room action at profiles/manager.py:672-677.

The recently-changed new-room path is the one that gets it RIGHT: `resolve_new_room_defaults` reads `builtins.get(profile_name)` raw and copies only declared fields (rooms/room_defaults.py:77-84), so a freshly created Roborock room correctly has no intensity from the brand — it is the profile-APPLY path that re-adds it.
survived.user_impact: Applying a room profile to a Roborock room stamps `clean_intensity="Quick"` — a value from a brand whose intensity option list (`clean_intensity_options`) is deliberately absent (adapters/roborock/adapter.py:241). The card's intensity chip row has no matching option to select, so the room shows a value the user cannot change or clear, and the "one source, no second vocabulary" contract that rooms/room_defaults.py was written to establish is broken on the second write path. Wire-inert today (Roborock's GenericRoomIdsEngine discards the Eufy-shaped payload, dispatch_engines.py:188-197), so no wrong physical action.

survived.title: A map rebuild silently auto-enables AND auto-approves rooms that never existed before, adding them to the clean queue unseen
survived.mechanism:
`rebuild_map_bucket` sets `previous = existing_rooms.get(room_id_key, {}) if preserve_existing_settings else {}` (line 148), then:
```
enabled=bool(previous.get("enabled", True)),
...
is_configured=bool(previous.get("is_configured", True)),
```
(lines 181, 197). For a room that is newly present in `discovered_rooms` and absent from `existing_rooms`, `previous` is `{}`, so BOTH defaults fire: the room enters `enabled=True, is_configured=True`.

`get_enabled_rooms_in_order` filters only on `bool(room.get("enabled", False))` (queue_engine.py:86-90) and there is no `is_configured` gate anywhere in the queue path — `is_configured` is consumed only by entity creation (entity_helpers.py:98) and the drift tracker (setup/drift.py:241). So the new room is in the queue immediately, ordered by `index` (map_manager.py:182).

The comment directly above these lines asserts the opposite behaviour: "a rebuild must PRESERVE whatever approval already existed — a rebuilt room must not read as unconfigured ... and equally must not silently auto-approve" (map_manager.py:160-165). It does silently auto-approve. `setup/drift.py:229-231` states the intended contract explicitly: "new rooms enter False and require the save_rooms step to flip them."
survived.user_impact: After a Rebuild Map, any segment that appeared since the last rebuild — a room the user renamed into existence in the vendor app, or on Eufy a phantom segment the CV segmenter split off — is cleaned on the next Start without ever appearing in the setup flow or the drift report. The user pressed Start expecting their configured room set and the robot cleans an extra room. With `preserve_existing_settings=False` the same two defaults apply to EVERY room, so the user's enable/disable selections are wholesale replaced by "everything on".

survived.title: apply_capability_gate and _protected_room_config hardcode Eufy display literals for the framework's 'no water' / 'default path' concepts
survived.mechanism:
`apply_capability_gate` — the capability gate the payload builder calls for every room (queue_engine.py:271-276) — writes brand literals directly rather than reading the catalog it was handed:
```
if not supports_mop and clean_mode in {"mop","vacuum_mop"}: ... water_level = "Off"   # line 509
if clean_mode == "vacuum": water_level = "Off"                                       # line 516
if not supports_water: water_level = "Off"                                           # line 520
if not supports_path: path_type = "wide"                                             # line 524
```
The function receives `catalog=` (line 477) and uses it for the mop-downgrade profile lookup at line 507, so the seam is present and simply not applied to these four assignments. `_protected_room_config` does the same twice (`protected["water_level"] = "Off"` at profiles/manager.py:104 and 108), and its output IS `effective_rooms` in the queue-construction path (run_plan.py:1309).

This is the exact defect the resolver was already fixed for: room_profiles.py:429-431 and 438-442 carry comments explaining that a literal `"Off"` "wrote Eufy casing into a Roborock resolution, where the value is 'off'" and that a strict `== "Off"` "meant this guard never fired on Roborock". The gate one function below was not given the same treatment.

On Roborock today the damage is absorbed: `_run_global_pre_calls` lowercases before the rank lookup (`value = str(room.get(field) or "").strip().lower()`, dispatch/manager.py:409), `_normalize_water_level_key` lowercases (run_plan.py:206), and the GenericRoomIdsEngine discards the water field entirely.
survived.user_impact: No wrong physical action on either shipped brand. survived.title: _SinglePhaseMixin silently swallows strict_order and the seam cannot express refusal — while the caller hides the order advisory on the strength of the request alone
survived.mechanism: `_SinglePhaseMixin.build_phases(self, *, strict_order=False, **kwargs)` returns `[self.build_payload(**kwargs)]` — `strict_order` is accepted, dropped on the floor, and nothing in the return value records that it was refused. The Protocol blesses this ("Engines that can't honor it (atomic batch shapes) ignore the flag", lines 93-97). Only GenericRoomIdsEngine overrides it; EufyRoomCleanEngine and DreameSegmentEngine inherit the swallow. The caller then treats the REQUEST as proof of enforcement: planning/run_plan.py:1458-1464 computes `order_advisory = None if strict_order else self._order_advisory(...)` using the raw parameter, not `effective_strict` and not any engine feedback, with the comment "Suppressed when strict_order is active — order is then ENFORCED (the sequenced per-room dispatch), so the advisory would contradict." `_order_advisory` (run_plan.py:697-723) returns its text precisely when `capabilities.honors_clean_order` is False — the exact brand class for which `_build_dispatch_phases` sets `effective_strict = bool(strict_order) and not honors_order` = True and therefore the one where an atomic engine's silent swallow bites. There is no field on the returned phase list (no `job_model`, no `strict_order_honored`) for the framework to check, so this cannot be detected downstream; it is a gap in the Protocol itself, not a missing call.
survived.user_impact: A brand that path-optimizes (honors_clean_order False) but whose payload shape is list-of-dicts or positional-arrays — i.e. anything on eufy_room_clean, dreame_room_clean, or a future engine built off _SinglePhaseMixin — gets ONE batch dispatch when the user asks for strict order. The rooms are cleaned in the device's optimized order, and the standing advisory that would have told the user 'this vacuum cleans in the order saved in its own app' is suppressed because they asked for strict order. The user is told order is enforced while it silently is not. Neither shipped brand hits this today (Eufy honors order so effective_strict folds to False and the advisory is None anyway; Roborock is on the overriding engine).

survived.title: Cancel is defeated by the phase watchdog: _cancel_in_flight is checked once, before two multi-second awaits, then the clean is dispatched unconditionally
survived.mechanism:
_run_advanced_phase checks the cancel flag at line 536-549 and then calls `await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)` (552-555). Inside _dispatch_active_phase there are three awaits before the send and NO re-check of `_cancel_in_flight`:
```
await self._manager._run_global_pre_calls(...)                 # blocking=True select.select_option to the device
await ...apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited(...)             # blocking=True vacuum.set_fan_speed
wire_payload = await self._manager._resolve_live_dispatch_payload(...)  # -> async_refresh_room_source -> roborock.get_maps, blocking=True, network
await self._manager._dispatch_clean_payload(...)               # fires regardless
```
Meanwhile jobs/active_job.py:2198-2215 sets `_cancel_in_flight = True` and `_phase_dispatch_pending = False` synchronously and then awaits `vacuum.return_to_base`. This is a genuine cross-await interleaving (a blocking service call and a network refresh), not a mid-synchronous-block race. survived.title: A raising dispatch kills the phase watchdog task and wedges the run in 'started' forever
survived.mechanism:
_run_advanced_phase's retry loop is:
```

    ...
    if not (initial and attempt == 1):
        await self._dispatch_active_phase(...)   # no try/except
    if await self._await_phase_started(...):
        self._clear_phase_dispatch_pending(...)
        return
```
_dispatch_active_phase can raise from three places: `_dispatch_clean_payload` -> hass.services.async_call(blocking=True) raises HomeAssistantError when the vacuum entity is unavailable or the brand integration rejects the command; `apply_per_room_live_settings_awaited` -> vacuum.set_fan_speed likewise; and on a zone phase `dispatch_zone_clean` raises ValueError by design for every cap violation (zone_max, degenerate rect, zone_min/max_area_m2, zone_min/max_side_m, unconvertible projection — dispatch/manager.py:109/118/122/131/151/158/169/173/223/228). _run_advanced_phase is only ever started via `hass.async_create_task(...)` (core/manager.py:5072, phase_runner.py:193) with no wrapper, so the exception ends the task. survived.title: The mixed-batch water SAFETY pre-call is best-effort — if it fails the clean still dispatches and the robot wet-mops the vacuum-only rooms
survived.mechanism:
_run_global_pre_calls ends every entry with:
```
try:
    await self._manager.hass.services.async_call(domain, service_name, {"entity_id": target_entity, value_key: wire_value}, blocking=True)
except Exception:
    _LOGGER.exception("global pre-call %s.%s failed for %s", ...)
```
and the caller then dispatches the clean regardless (core/manager.py:5005-5023; phase_runner.py:1010-1027). For a plain fan pre-call "best-effort" is defensible. For the `mixed_mode_water_policy: "safest"` entry it is not: that entry IS the safety mechanism. The docstring states the contract — "a device-GLOBAL water/mop-intensity select can't be zeroed per-room, so a mixed mop + vacuum-only batch that max-wins to the strongest water would WET-MOP the dry (vacuum-only) rooms" — and the whole mitigation is the one select_option call at 436. Exact batch: an S7/S8 (mop_settable True, adapters/roborock/adapter.py:132-153), rooms Kitchen `clean_mode=mop, water_level=high` and Bedroom `clean_mode=vacuum`; `_mop_rooms=1`, `len=2`, `_mixed_batch` True, `_use_safest` True, `best_index=0`, `canonical_value="off"`, target `select.<obj>_mop_intensity`. Verified by direct execution against the real module: appending a single (nan, 0.5, 0.0, 0.0) correspondence to a clean 8-point set yields coeffs (nan,)*6 and resid 0.0. The dispatch then fails at dispatch/manager.py:186 `int(round(x0))`, which raises ValueError('cannot convert float NaN to integer').
killed.user_impact: No wrong dispatch — it fails closed by accident, at the wrong layer. The user gets 'Failed to start zone clean: cannot convert float NaN to integer' instead of the designed 'could not place the drawn zone on the device coordinate frame ... refusing to dispatch', which is the message that tells them to re-open the map. The documented safety contract ('the fit ... is then round-trip VALIDATED ... returns None and the caller MUST refuse', zone_dispatch.py:11-15) is not the thing that stopped it.
killed.guards_checked: (1) _solve3_two:36 singularity check — verified non-firing for NaN. (2) fit_normalized_to_mm:53-59 input filter — `float(c[i])` accepts float('nan') without raising, so a NaN correspondence is not dropped. (3) normalized_rects_to_mm:116-120 both refuse-gates — coeffs is not None and residual is 0.0, both pass. (4) The upstream producer clamps but does not NaN-filter: mapping/map_source_runtime.py:551-557 appends `(p[0], p[1], float(mx), float(my))` for any p the projector returns. (5) dispatch/manager.py:155-161 mm_rects-is-None refusal — never reached.
killed.area: AREA 5 — ZONE CLEAN (dispatch/manager.py::dispatch_zone_clean + all of dispatch/zone_dispatch.py)
killed_by: The arithmetic is right (abs(nan) < 1e-9 is False so _solve3_two:36 does not treat a NaN determinant as singular; max() keeps the incumbent against NaN so max_residual_mm returns 0.0) but there is no producer that can deliver a NaN correspondence. correspondences_from_mapdata (map_source_runtime.py:544-556) appends (p[0], p[1], float(mx), float(my)) where mx/my are the parser's integer Room bbox coords and p comes from proj(), whose last operation is _clamp01(p.x/img_w) — and _clamp01 collapses NaN to 0.0 by the same max()/min() semantics the finding relies on. img_w/img_h are guarded > 0 at 457. So the injected-NaN reproduction is synthetic, not a real input. Even granting it, the outcome is fail-closed (ValueError at int(round(nan))), i.e. a worse error message rather than a wrong dispatch.
confirmations: Code facts confirmed by reading zone_dispatch.py:31-120. `abs(d) < 1e-9` is False for NaN so _solve3_two does not treat a NaN determinant as singular; fit_normalized_to_mm's float(c[i]) accepts float('nan') without raising (57-59); and max_residual_mm's `worst = max(worst, ...)` keeps the 0.0 incumbent because every comparison against NaN is False, so the 119 refuse-gate passes. The dispatch then dies at dispatch/manager.py:186 int(round(x0)). The finding is honest that it fails closed and that the only cost is the wrong error message. Reachability (a NaN correspondence from the projector) is unproven, which is exactly why LOW is the right rating.

verifier_notes:
3 of 38 killed; 5 severity corrections. Patterns worth the orchestrator's attention:

(1) TWO findings died on ONE premise, and a third finding in the same set already contained the refutation. DQ-ACT-4 and DQ-PH-4 both claim start_selected_rooms dispatches an empty room_clean for a zone-first plan; both explicitly dismissed get_start_status as "not a guard here". DQ-Q-3 — a different finder, same seam — proves the opposite: phases[0] with room_count 0 hits build_start_blocker_from_lifecycle's `payload_room_count <= 0` and blocks the start outright. The blocker tests payload count SEPARATELY from queue count, which is what both finders missed. When two findings at one line disagree about whether a guard fires, that is the cheapest thing to check first.

(2) DQ-PAY-3 died on a dataclass default. Its whole chain needed the stored room to LACK a clean_intensity key. Every room-creation path in the codebase builds through RoomConfig and emits asdict(), so the key is always present as "" — rooms/room_manager.py:104 and maps/map_manager.py:188 both write `str(_default("clean_intensity", ""))`. The finder read room_defaults.py (which correctly omits the field from the BRAND defaults) and inferred the field was absent from the ROOM. Same trap partially caught DQ-Q-4, whose cited line-209 fallback also never fires on the production apply path. Rule of thumb for this codebase: a stored room has every RoomConfig field, always — "the brand omits it" never means "the room lacks the key".

(3) Duplicate pairs that must be deduped before work is assigned, or the same fix gets scoped twice: DQ-PAY-4 == DQ-ZONE-1 (identical, dispatch/manager.py Eufy zone repeat clamp — note DQ-PAY-4's headline is wrong, the default of 3 is not applied, NO clamp runs at all); DQ-ACT-1 and DQ-DE-1 are one line (dispatch/manager.py:317) with DQ-DE-1 being strictly more reachable — one renamed room versus a total slug miss; DQ-Q-1(a) and DQ-DE-5(a) are the same dead `queue_room_ids` union.

(4) The single strongest verified finding is DQ-DE-1: a one-target strict-order phase makes `dropped != []` logically equivalent to `new_segments == []`, so the "live source unavailable, fall back to stored ids" branch fires for a target that was resolved and REJECTED. Roborock renumbers segment ids by design, so one renamed room means the robot cleans a different physical room, and the watchdog then re-dispatches the same stale id up to max_attempts. That is three wrong-room cleans from a single rename.

(5) Comments-as-false-claims recurred and every instance held up under reading: map_manager.py:160-165 says a rebuild "must not silently auto-approve" (it does, DQ-Q-5); registry.py:428-431 says an unknown template "is rejected at registration" (it is a warning, DQ-DE-4); phase_runner.py:1028-1030 says an empty segment list means the room was skipped (it means stale ids were sent, DQ-DE-1); run_plan.py:806-808 says phase 0 is always a real clean the initial dispatch can send (a zone is not, DQ-Q-3). The methodology rule earned its place again.

(6) DQ-ACT-2 is the one finding I checked hardest against the single-event-loop rule and it survives: the cancel flag is read once at phase_runner.py:536 and there are three genuine suspension points before the send (two blocking service calls and a network get_maps). Not a mid-synchronous-block race. Downgraded to HIGH only because the window is seconds per phase transition, not a standing condition.

(7) Severity discipline: I downgraded DQ-Q-4, DQ-PAY-6 and DQ-ZONE-5 because each has a real code fact but no demonstrated wrong result — vocabulary that is rescued downstream by case-insensitive comparison, or a UX half-shipped. All three are worth fixing; none should compete for budget with DQ-DE-1, DQ-ACT-3 or DQ-PH-1.

34 of 38 findings reproduce; 4 do not. Patterns across the set:

(1) THREE FINDINGS DESCRIBE THE SAME ZONE-FIRST CODE AND ONLY ONE IS RIGHT. DQ-ACT-4 and DQ-PH-4 both claim an empty room_clean is dispatched to the device; DQ-Q-3 claims the start is blocked. DQ-Q-3 is correct — start_selected_rooms calls get_start_status first (core/manager.py:4937), which builds the identical plan through the peek path and blocks on payload_room_count==0. Neither ACT-4 nor PH-4 traced the caller above their entry point. Both were also authored with detailed "guards checked" lists that omitted get_start_status entirely, which is how a preflight-blocked path got reported twice as a wire dispatch.

(2) THE ROOMCONFIG DATACLASS IS THE MOST-MISSED RESCUE. RoomConfig.as_dict() is asdict(), so EVERY per-room field is always present in storage, including clean_intensity="" and water_level="". That single fact refutes DQ-PAY-3 outright and neuters half of DQ-Q-4 and DQ-PAY-6. Notably DQ-Q-4 correctly listed it as a guard and DQ-PAY-3 then contradicted it — the finder set is internally inconsistent about the one fact that decides three findings. Any fix wave should establish "the stored room always carries every key" as a shared premise before touching the resolver.

(3) THE REAL CLUSTER IS TWO LINES, NOT TWENTY. dispatch/manager.py:317 (stale-id fallback) accounts for both CRITICALs — DQ-DE-1 is far more reachable than DQ-ACT-1 because a strict-order phase has exactly one target, which makes "one room dropped" and "nothing resolved" the same condition. And profiles/manager.py:225 (get_room_profiles with no catalog) accounts for DQ-PAY-1, DQ-Q-2, and the real-world outcome DQ-Q-4 misattributed to room_profiles.py:209. Fixing those two lines closes five findings including both CRITICALs.

(4) THE FINDERS DID NOT MODEL apply_run_profile. DQ-Q-1's headline impact ("bedrooms vacuumed at max instead of quiet") does not reproduce, because profiles/manager.py:1236-1240 persists each group room's settings onto the stored room before the run starts, so the global effective_rooms view the collapse falls back to already carries them. What genuinely survives is narrower and more interesting: a room named in TWO groups is dispatched once with the last group's settings, so the vacuum-then-mop-the-same-room profile silently loses its first pass. That is the case _build_steps_phases exists to serve.

(5) SEVERITY INFLATION IS CONCENTRATED IN FUTURE-BRAND FINDINGS AND IN CARD-IMPACT CLAIMS. Three MEDIUMs (DQ-PAY-5, DQ-PAY-6, DQ-DE-3) are LOW: none is reachable on a shipped install and none is a seam the config categorically cannot express (DQ-DE-3's "command": None works today). DQ-PAY-6's card claim specifically fails because the water chip row is mop-gated (room-editor.js:260-262) and _protected_room_config only stamps "Off" on non-mop rooms — the row is hidden in exactly the case that gets the bad value. Findings that assert a frontend consequence should be checked against the renderer; DQ-ZONE-5 did this correctly (verified by grep) and DQ-PAY-6 did not.

(6) ONE FINDING WAS REPRODUCED SYNTHETICALLY RATHER THAN FROM A REAL INPUT. DQ-ZONE-6's NaN arithmetic is correct but no producer can emit NaN: _clamp01 collapses NaN to 0.0 by the very max()/min() semantics the finding relies on, and the mm side is integer bbox coords. Executing a function against hand-injected values is not reachability.

Highest-confidence real defects, ranked: DQ-DE-1 (wrong physical room, Roborock, three times), DQ-ACT-1 (same line), DQ-PAY-1 (Roborock profile choice has zero effect on suction, silently), DQ-PAY-2 (empty water_level on the Eufy wire from a granite/concrete mop room), DQ-ACT-3 (one transient service error wedges the run forever; deterministic for an oversized saved zone), DQ-PH-1/PH-2/PH-3 (the phased-run recording trio — every stepped run's learning, missed-room report and per-room history is wrong, and PH-2 permanently mislabels healthy rooms as trouble).
